sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance that can never be duplicated or reinstantiated.
sketches.resonance: Declaring grief as an object means there is only one, it exists forever, and no matter where you reference it, it is always the same one.

sketches.mechanism: The `Maybe` type wrapping a value that is destructured reveals `Nothing` — pattern matching forces you to confront the absent case.
sketches.resonance: You reach for what someone left you and the language forces you to handle the possibility that there is nothing there.
sketches.draft:
whatYouLeftMe :: Maybe a
whatYouLeftMe = Nothing

unwrap :: Maybe a -> Maybe a
unwrap (Just x) = Just x
unwrap Nothing  = Nothing

sketches.mechanism: A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table even when no match exists in the right, filling unmatched columns with NULL.
sketches.resonance: One table remembers everything; the other has no corresponding row — the join preserves the memory but returns absence.
